newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria not interested in Israeli ideas, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Syria not interested in Israeli ideas, paper says.

text.p: Syria is not interested in the latest ideas put forward by Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu to resume peace talks because they ignore withdrawal from the Golan Heights, an official newspaper said on Friday.
It was the first reaction from Damascus to talks between the Israeli Prime Minister and U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Thursday.

The daily Al-Thawra daily: "It is important to remind here that all the formulas and proposals carried by the head of the extremist rightist Israeli government, or what is called compromises, to resume the peace negotiations on the Syrian track.. will fall down.
"These proposals return the peace process to the zero point, ignore the land-for-peace principle and approve the Israeli concept which aims at combining occupation and peace.."

The daily added that the proposals also aimed at relieving the current Israeli government from the commitments and understanding reached with the previous Labour-led Israeli government before the talks broke off in March last year.
Syria says the previous Israeli government which lost to Netanyahu's Likud party in elections last May agreed to withdraw from the Golan, captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
Netanyahu gave no indication in Washington that he was prepared to soften his stand on withdrawal from the strategic heights.
"We have a stated position," he told reporters. "It is clear that we think the Golan Heights is crucial, vital territory for the defence of Israel. And that position has not changed."
In Jerusalem, Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said Netanyahu had proposed a "creative" formula to restart the Syrian talks, but declined to elaborate.
Another official daily, Al-Baath, reiterated Syria's readiness to resume the peace talks with Israel immediately if Israel accepted withdrawal from the Golan.
